newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Khmer Rouge radio fails to broadcast.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Khmer Rouge radio fails to broadcast.

text.p: Khmer Rouge guerrilla radio, the rebels' strident propaganda mouthpiece, failed to broadcast its regular bulletin on Thursday morning.
The clandestine radio usually broadcasts for 90 minutes in the morning and again in the evening from the guerrillas' northern zone of control.
Broadcasts have been known to cease for short periods and resume without explanation, apparently due to technical problems.
But the last time the radio went off the air, in mid-June, the cause was a violent split in the secretive group's leadership which led to the purging of supreme leader Pol Pot late last month.
The radio failed to broadcast for about a week at that time and then resumed without explanation.
In recent weeks the radio has directed a stream of criticism at Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted his rival co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, in a bloody power-grab early last month.

The rebels have labelled Hun Sen a puppet of Vietnam and have called for united opposition to his rule, while Hun Sen has warned of military action against the rebels in their Anlong Veng base in the remote north of the country.
On Wednesday the radio said Ranariddh was still the country's legal first prime minister and a move to approve a new premier was a political game.
Later on Wednesday the National Assembly voted by the required two-thirds majority to approve the nomination of Foreign Minister Ung Huot as first prime minister.
The rebels boycotted a 1993 election organised by the United Nations and fought a low-intensity guerrilla war against the coalition government which emerged from the poll.
More than a million Cambodians died during Pol Pot's 1975-79 "killing fields" rule.
